name: Mix pads for role, EQ clarity, energy, and width control
goal: Mix pads based on role (lead ambient vs background glue): infinite-average spectrum to see occupied bands, high-pass to protect kick/bass, filter reverb/delay lows (~100 Hz), manage mids/highs vs vocals with dynamic/sidechain EQ sparingly, automate filter/FX for section energy, and narrow stereo (or multiband width) when pads crowd the image.

source.title: 5 Tips for Mixing Pads and Synths for a Full, Clear Sound

prerequisites: DAW with EQ, spectrum analyzer, optional multiband imager, pads already sound-designed

outputs.name: mix_ready_pad_bus
outputs.description: Pad bus that supports the mix without mud

constraints: Ground every step in the source YouTube-provided captions; do not invent UI or settings.
Original synthesis only — map brand UI (Serum/Vital/Pigments/Phase Plant/etc.) to portable osc/filter/FX roles for a browser or generic hybrid synth; never rip presets, wavetables, or samples.
Prefer transferable signal-flow and motion relationships over vendor-specific preset names.
Educational mixing procedure — tool names in the video are examples; use any EQ/imager with the same moves.
Avoid extreme dynamic EQ pumping that destroys pad ambience.

steps.action: Decide pad role (lead evolving bed vs background atmosphere) — mix moves follow the role.
View long-average spectrum to see which bands the pad occupies vs vocals/keys.
High-pass the pad to leave room for kick/bass; stop before the pad thins excessively; likewise HP reverb/delay returns (~100 Hz) to prevent buildup.
In busy mids/highs, use gentle tonal EQ or dynamic EQ sidechained to conflicting elements (e.g. snare/vocal) only as needed.
Automate mute/filter/FX across intro/verse/chorus so pads shape energy while staying supportive.
If pads steal stereo space: collapse toward mono and pan, or multiband-narrow only conflicting bands while keeping air wide.

verification: Kick/bass hit harder after pad HP
Pad still fills its intended role
No obvious pumping from overdone dynamic EQ
